transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
President Trump is shifting Vice President J.D. Vance's focus from the Iran war to tackling
corruption and crime in Democratic-controlled parts of the U.S.
Trump said in a social media post, "We don't need to deal with Iran.
Those days have long since passed."
Meanwhile, President Trump says he wants former Apple CEO Tim Cook to be the CEO of
Nvidia.
After the resignation of Jensen Wong, Wong has been close to Trump and traveled with
him to China.
NPR's Danielle Kurtzleben has more.
On social media this morning, Trump wrote that Wong has done "a fantastic job."
He added, "There is only one man to take his place, Tim Cook of Apple.
A legend replaces a legend."
Wong announced his resignation after news reports alleging that he had had an extramarital
affair with one of the company's clients, who U.S. intelligence officials concluded had
been recruited by China's top spy agency.
Wong has had the president's ear for much of this term, demonstrated in September when
Trump called Wong's phone while Wong was on stage at a conference.
He also joined Trump on a state visit to the U.K. last year and to China this year.
Danielle Kurtzleben, NPR News, The White House.
The U.S. servicemen arrested in the U.K. on suspicion of espionage is an Army Lieutenant
Colonel.
NPR's Quill Lawrence reports he was caught in a sting by British authorities.
The 41-year-old Army Lieutenant Colonel currently being held by U.K. Metropolitan Police has
served nearly 20 years and had deployed to Iraq and Afghanistan.
A U.S. Army counterintelligence command spokesman confirms to NPR that the suspect was caught
in a sting, where he didn't know he was speaking to British agents.
U.K. authorities allege he was attempting to share sensitive information with Russia.
He's currently being held in London and will be charged early next week, and then transferred
to American custody and charged under the Uniform Code of Military Justice.
In recent weeks, U.S. bases in the U.K. have been on high alert for possible attacks linked
to the war in Iran.
But British authorities say this case is not related.
Quill Lawrence, NPR News.
The Senate race in Mississippi has come to an end, with Democrat Scott Colome narrowly
taking the seat from Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith.
Hundreds gathered at historically black Tougaloo College in Jackson to celebrate the win.
P.R. Jackson, with Mississippi Public Broadcasting, has reactions.
Senator Scott Colome is the first black person to be elected to the U.S. Senate for Mississippi
in nearly 150 years.
NAACP President Derrick Johnson says Colome's victory was driven by Mississippians wanting
to see change.
The public policy that governs our lives will come through the U.S. Senate, and I'm glad
we have someone who's willing to listen and execute effectively.
Colome campaigned aggressively on increasing the federal minimum wage.
Mississippians say his win is just the beginning toward getting the state's voice heard in
Washington, D.C.
For NPR News, I'm T.A.R. Jackson, and Jackson.
The U.S. stock market fell today, and oil prices climbed.
This is NPR News.
The gunman suspected of killing a man at a busy Washington, D.C., gym this morning before
fleeing and shooting four more people has been identified as a medical doctor locked
in a dispute with building management over mold and moisture problems in his penthouse.
Authorities say the gunman fatally shot himself inside an apartment where he'd been speaking
by phone to police negotiators.
Broadway's spring season is going to be filled with Hollywood stars.
As Jeff London reports, the big-ticket celebrities are coming with big-ticket costs.
Steve Carell and John C. Reilly will star in a revival of Neil Simon's The Odd Couple,
and Jessica Chastain will star in a new play about an actress with dementia.
Also opening this spring is Julie Roberts with Paul Rudd in Small Mouth Sounds, a comic
and touching play where hardly anyone speaks.
These productions will be open for limited runs, and given the limited supply of seats
available, ticket prices are high.
If you want to see Julia Roberts from the best seats, be prepared to fork out almost
$650.
For NPR News, I'm Jeff London in New York.
Chicago Cubs center fielder Pete Crow Armstrong has won the National League's MVP award unanimously
after the center fielder wowed in a majestic all-around season with 45 home runs, 41 steals
and 107 runs batted in, and Houston Astros slugger Yordan Alvarez is the unanimous American
League MVP, hitting a career-high 316 batting average with 42 homers and 106 RBIs.
This is NPR News from Washington.

topics.text: Trump shifts Vance's focus from Iran war to corruption and crime in Democratic cities
Trump says Tim Cook should replace Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO after Huang's resignation
Army Lieutenant Colonel arrested in U.K. on suspicion of espionage, allegedly sharing secrets with Russia
Democrat Scott Colome narrowly wins Mississippi Senate seat over Republican Cindy Hyde-Smith
U.S. stock market falls and oil prices climb
Gunman kills man at Washington, D.C. gym, wounds four, then dies by suicide during police negotiations
Broadway spring season features Hollywood stars with high ticket prices, including Julia Roberts
Pete Crow-Armstrong wins unanimous National League MVP; Yordan Alvarez wins American League MVP
